title: Pipeline checks
summary: Order a continuous integration pipeline so failures stop before deployment.

scenario.briefing: The campus CI pipeline has the right checks but the wrong order. A failed test currently deploys before anyone notices. Put verification before release.

objectives.description: Explain why cheap checks run before expensive ones.
Check understanding through the remaining explanation and transfer evidence.

hints: Start by obtaining the exact source revision.
Install reproducibly, then run static checks and tests.
Build only after checks pass, and deploy only after a successful build.
Order: checkout, frozen install, lint, typecheck, test, content validate, build, deploy.

misconceptions.description: Deploying before static checks and tests run.
misconceptions.feedback: Deploying before checks publishes unverified code. Run lint, typecheck, tests, and content checks before build and deploy.

misconceptions.description: Installing the newest matching versions in CI.
misconceptions.feedback: Installing latest versions makes the pipeline depend on the clock. Use a frozen lockfile install.

misconceptions.description: Treating a green pipeline as proof the change is correct.
misconceptions.feedback: A green run proves the configured checks passed. It does not prove the feature is correct or safe to deploy.

sections.title: CI is a gate
sections.body: Continuous integration runs repeatable checks on every change. The pipeline should stop at the first failure, preserve logs, and prevent unreviewed artifacts from reaching deployment. The same revision should flow through every stage.

sections.title: Order by cost and risk
sections.body: Cheap checks such as lint and types fail fast before slower tests and builds. Content validation and security checks belong before release. A pipeline that reports success without executing its checks is worse than no pipeline.

vocabulary.definition: Continuous integration: automated checks on changes.
An install that uses exact locked dependency versions.
Stop at the earliest reliable failure.

steps.title: Order the pipeline
steps.prompt: Arrange the stages so a failing check stops the pipeline before deployment.

items.label: Build the web and server artifacts

steps.explanation: Acquire the revision, install reproducibly, run fast checks, run tests and content validation, build, then deploy. Any failure stops the chain.
hints: Start by getting the exact source revision.
Install from the lockfile before running checks.
Fast static checks should fail before slower tests and builds.
Order: checkout, install, lint, typecheck, test, content, build, deploy.

steps.title: Why a frozen lockfile?
steps.prompt: Why does CI install dependencies with a frozen lockfile?

options.label: It reproduces the exact dependency versions recorded for the project.
It always installs faster than every other method.
It upgrades every dependency to the latest version.

quiz.explanation: A frozen lockfile makes installs reproducible, so CI checks the same dependency graph that was reviewed.

hints: The lockfile records exact versions and integrity hashes.
A frozen install refuses to rewrite the lockfile.
Speed and freshness are not the goal of CI installation.
Choose reproducibility from the recorded dependency versions.

steps.title: Pipeline evidence

statements.label: A failed check should stop later stages.
The tested and deployed revision should be the same artifact.
A script that exits zero without running checks is acceptable.
Failure logs should be preserved for diagnosis.

steps.explanation: A gate is only useful if it stops release and preserves evidence when it fails.
hints: A green pipeline is evidence about the checks it ran.
The same commit and lockfile should produce the same dependency set.
Deployment is a separate, reversible step.
Select stopping on failure, reproducible installs, and retained logs; reject green as proof of correctness.

accessibility.summary: Pipeline stages can be reordered with buttons and read as an ordered list.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Use move buttons; drag is optional. Arrow keys select quiz options.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: Each stage announces its position after every move. The quiz explanation is read after submission.
